findings.claim: The whole-segment redirection strip (fold 1 item 5) is quote-blind: the tokenizer discards quoting, so a QUOTED argument whose token matches the operator regexes is dropped, and because the strip runs before the value-flag pairing the flag then swallows the PR target — a regression against main and the pre-fold head that re-creates the fabricated-target class F5 was chartered to remove, and breaks the invariant the suite names ('a value-taking flag does not swallow the PR target').
findings.counterexample:
bash: `gh pr merge -b "
" 5` merges PR 5. Projection: main and e152e37b {pr: 5}; fold head {pr: null, branch: 'feat/demo'}; `gh pr merge -b "
" --repo owner/name 5` → {repo: '', pr: null, branch: 'owner/name'}. FOLDED (fold 2): a per-token literal flag; the strip skips literal tokens; four rows and the widened invariant row.

findings.claim: The fold-1 residue sentence says only the last three of the five `&`/`|`-carrying operators are merges the shell runs; all five run the merge, so the strict bypass surface is understated by two, and the test corpus comment classifies `>|` and `2>&1` as mutants (shapes the shell does not run).
findings.counterexample: bash with a stub: `>| out.txt gh pr merge 5` → GH-RAN (also under noclobber); `2>&1 gh pr merge 5` → GH-RAN; the wrapper projects nothing for any of the five. FOLDED (fold 2): both sentences corrected; the two rows relabelled as locked disclosed misses.

findings.claim: The 'PowerShell line continuation (a trailing backtick)' bullet sits in the disclosed-MISS list whose header says the gate does not fire and every entry is a locked row; the gate DOES fire (with a bogus `unresolvedTarget: '`'` — strict denies a bogus target, pilot warns and lets PR 5 merge unjudged), no row locks it, and it is not new (main projects the identical payload).
findings.counterexample: pwsh 7: a script `gh pr merge `<LF>5` with a gh.cmd stub → GH-RAN pr merge 5. Committed hook with a PowerShell envelope: exit 0, CLI spawned, payload {pr: null, unresolvedTarget: '`'}; main in a vm sandbox: the same. FOLDED (fold 2): a ps-mode continuation arm (backtick-newline joins the word, the twin of the bash backslash-newline arm), rows, the bullet removed.

findings.claim: The `flags` cure of fold 1 item 3 applies to `time` alone; every other table word skips an unknown `-` token as a flag, so the wrapper projects a merge for command lines on which the program runs nothing (invalid option) — the false-deny class, undisclosed.
findings.counterexample: `command -x gh pr merge 5` → 'invalid option', nothing runs; `timeout -Z 30 …`, `nice -Z …`, `env -Z …`, `nohup -x …`, `exec -x …` likewise; the seam projects [['5']] for each. FOLDED (fold 2): ruled a disclosed FALSE FIRE with rows — a closed flags list per program would turn every real flag it omitted into a miss, the wrong direction.

findings.claim: The hook's load-bearing exit-code contract header enumerates every exit-2 cause and is byte-identical to main's, but the branch added two exit-2 arms (the spent budget; the stdin timer) that it does not name.
findings.counterexample: diff of lines 1–25 between main's hook and the committed hook: identical; a not-applicable `echo hi` envelope with the pipe held open exits 2 at 1 057 ms, which the header promises exit 0 for. FOLDED (fold 2): the header names both arms.

findings.claim: The `env -S` residue bullet states a mechanism the code does not use for `--split-string=`: only `-S` is in env's operand list; the `=` spelling is skipped as an ordinary flag and the operand SURVIVES; in both spellings the miss comes from the anchor failing on a single quoted word.
findings.counterexample: TRANSPARENT_WRAPPERS.env.operand = ['-u','-C','-S','--unset','--chdir']; `env --split-string='gh pr merge 5'` → no projection (right outcome, wrong stated reason); bash `env -S "gh pr merge 5"` → GH-RAN. FOLDED (fold 2): the sentence corrected; `--split-string` joins the operand list.
